# Temple Scroll Column 52 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 52 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 52:3 — "send her away" vs. "divorce her" vs. "divorce her"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "send her away" | Literal shalach — the Hebrew verb for divorce is literally "to send away" |
| LOGOS | "divorce her" | Standard English legal term conveying the same concept |
| PNEUMA | "divorce her" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "divorce" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). While "send away" is literal, "divorce" clearly communicates the legal action in English without loss of meaning.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 52:5 — "disgraceful-thing" vs. "outrage" vs. "shameful act"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "disgraceful-thing" | Literal nevalah — a strong term for moral outrage in Israel |
| LOGOS | "outrage" | Concise rendering capturing the severity of the Hebrew term |
| PNEUMA | "shameful act" | Accessible modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "outrage" (LOGOS). The term nevalah in Israelite legal contexts denotes a grave violation of community norms; "outrage" captures this gravity better than "shameful act."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 52:5 — "burn out" vs. "purge" vs. "root out"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "burn out the evil" | Literal bi'arta — from the root b-'-r meaning "to burn/consume" |
| LOGOS | "purge the evil" | Standard Deuteronomic formula in English scholarship |
| PNEUMA | "root out the evil" | Active English verb conveying thorough removal |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "purge" (LOGOS). This is the standard rendering of the Deuteronomic purge formula across major English translations.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 52:14 — "uncover the skirt" vs. "uncover the garment" vs. "dishonor his father"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "uncover the skirt of his father" | Literal kenaf — "wing/skirt/corner" of the garment |
| LOGOS | "uncover his father's garment" | Standard euphemistic rendering preserving the metaphor |
| PNEUMA | "dishonor his father in this way" | Interprets the euphemism for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "uncover his father's garment" (LOGOS). The euphemism should be preserved as it is in the Hebrew text; PNEUMA's interpretation, while correct, removes the metaphorical language.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 52:15 — anatomical literalism vs. standard vs. modern

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "crushed of testicle or cut of male-member" | Hyper-literal anatomical Hebrew |
| LOGOS | "emasculated by crushing or cutting" | Standard scholarly rendering preserving both methods |
| PNEUMA | "castrated, whether by crushing or cutting" | Modern medical term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. EMET's anatomical literalism is unnecessarily graphic; PNEUMA's "castrated" is too narrow (the Hebrew includes broader forms of genital injury). "Emasculated" preserves the legal scope.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 52:16 — "bastard" vs. "illegitimate birth" vs. "forbidden union"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "bastard" | Traditional English rendering of mamzer |
| LOGOS | "one of illegitimate birth" | Precise legal status without pejorative overtone |
| PNEUMA | "one born of a forbidden union" | Explanatory rendering focusing on the cause |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "illegitimate birth" (LOGOS). "Bastard" carries modern pejorative connotations beyond the legal meaning; PNEUMA's rendering, while accurate, is more interpretive than translational.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
